sections.COMMENTS:
This Composite Source straddles the Apulia Swell, part of the Neogene-Quaternary foreland (namely the Apulia Foreland) between two opposite-verging chains: the SW-verging Albanides-Hellenides, and the NE-verging southern Apennines, merging southwardly with the SSE-verging Calabrian Arc.
Several authors analyzed the structural setting of the Apulia Foreland (Gambini and Tozzi, 1996; Doglioni et al., 1999; Catalano et al., 2000; Argnani et al., 2001; Finetti and Del Ben, 2005; Tondi et al., 2005; Billi et al., 2007; Nicolai and Gambini, 2007; Butler, 2009; Del Ben, 2009; Volpi et al., 2011; Del Ben et al., 2015; Milia et al., 2017; Volpi et al., 2017; Teofilo et al., 2018), which is considered the peripheral bulge produced by flexural bending due to the loading of the two confronting chains. For a number of authors, this bending was responsible for an extensional tectonic regime unfolding during the Pliocene-Quaternary that generated NW-SE trending normal faults (Ciaranfi et al., 1988; Argnani et al., 2001; Finetti and Del Ben, 2005).
The NW-SE extensional faults previously recognized in the Apulia Swell pertain to a major fault system with remarkable evidence of recent (Pliocene-Holocene) tectonic activity, referred to as the South Apulia Fault System (SAFS, Maesano et al., 2020). The geometry of the SAFS is documented in detail by high resolution bathymetric data and by multiscale analysis of seismic profiles (from high penetration to sub-bottom CHIRP; Maesano et al., 2020).
The SAFS, which can be followed for a length of at least 100 km, determined the formation of two elongated basins (Northern Basin and Southern Basin), separated by a prominent horst (Central Horst). Two main faults bound the Northern and Southern Basin respectively and are associated with various other antithetic and synthetic secondary structures. The major faults forming the SAFS extend at least down to 12 km depth, reaching the top of the lower Triassic succession and possibly rooting in the Permian-Triassic succession (Maesano et al., 2020).
Seismicity within the Apulia Foreland is scarce and sparse, in agreement with the characteristics of a stable continental region. Nonetheless, this area hosted the 20 February 1743 (Mw 6.7) Ionio Settentrionale earthquake and a small sequence in 1974 (Rovida et al., 2021), with Mw 5.0 for the mainshock and a transpressive focal mechanism (Favali et al., 1990), accounting for an ~NE-SW shortening. Recently (2013-2014), some small events were recorded in the Apulia Swell, with Ml of the strongest ones ranging between 3.1 and 3.7, and depth between 5 and 10 km (ISIDe Working Group, 2007).
The 20 February 1743 earthquake heavily damaged the Salento Peninsula and the Ionian Islands (Greece) and was widely felt all over the Ionian and Adriatic regions (Galli and Naso, 2008; Guidoboni et al., 2019). It also caused a tsunami that was observed in the Brindisi harbor (Scalese, 1743; Iurlaro, 1978; Margottini, 1981; Guidoboni et al., 2019) and is supposed to have affected the southeastern coast of the Salento Peninsula (Mastronuzzi et al., 2007). However, its actual location is poorly known because of the dearth of macroseismic data in the near field.
The dip-slip component of the SAFS activity is predominant and well documented by both the morpho-bathymetric and the seismic reflection data. Nonetheless, the evidence of a possible horizontal component of motion is not negligible and is suggested by the right-stepping arrangement of the northern and southern main faults making up the SAFS. The system can thus be interpreted as the result of the activity of a deep-seated left-lateral shear zone in a transtensive tectonic context (Maesano et al., 2020). The presence of a left-lateral component along the SAFS would be in agreement with the few focal mechanisms recorded in the area, which indicate a left-lateral mechanism on the NW-SE nodal planes (Favali et al., 1990; MuÃ§o, 1994; Pondrelli and Salimbeni, 2006).
Throw rate estimates for the northern and southern main faults making up the SAFS were proposed adopting a probabilistic approach, following the method proposed by Zechar and Frankel (2009).
